facts.statement: Juehuaornis was an extinct ornithuromorph dinosaur that lived in present-day China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Juehuaornis is an extinct genus of ornithuromorph dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of present-day China.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen SJG 00001 was discovered near Lingyuan in the Aptian-aged Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, SJG 00001, was found near Lingyuan in a layer of the Jiufotang Formation dating from the Aptian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of an almost complete, associated skeleton with a skull and preserved feather remains.
facts.quote: It consists of an almost complete and associated skeleton with skull, compressed on a plate. It preserves feather remains.

facts.statement: The species Juehuaornis zhangi was named and described in 2015 by Wang Ren-fe, Wang Yan, and Hu Dongyu.
facts.quote: In 2015, the type species Juehuaornis zhangi was named and described by Wang Ren-fe, Wang Yan and Hu Dongyu.

facts.statement: The genus name Juehuaornis combines the name of Juehua Island, known as "Chrysanthemum Island" off Liaoning, with the Greek word for bird.
facts.quote: The generic name combines a reference to the island of Juehua, the "Chrysanthemum Island" off the coast of Liaoning, with a Greek ὄρνις, ornis, "bird".

facts.statement: The specific name zhangi honors the curator Zhang Dayong.
facts.quote: The specific name honours curator Zhang Dayong.

facts.statement: Juehuaornis possessed a very long beak that reached 70% of the total skull length.
facts.quote: Juehuaornis has a long beak which reaches 70% of the total skull length.

facts.statement: Juehuaornis was classified within the Ornithuromorpha in 2015.
facts.quote: Juehuaornis was placed in the Ornithuromorpha in 2015.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Juehuaornis should be considered the same genus as Changzuiornis and Dingavis, which would grant Juehuaornis priority.
facts.quote: In 2016 it was suggested that Juehuaornis might be cogeneric to the closely related genera Changzuiornis and Dingavis found in the same formation, in which case Juehuaornis would have priority.

facts.statement: Fossils of Juehuaornis date from the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
